description: This image displays three pie charts representing the problem distribution based on correctness under "w/ knowledge" and "w/o knowledge" settings using a Zero-Shot approach, categorized into three difficulty levels labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard." A single shared legend on the right identifies four categories represented in each chart: a teal slice labeled "N+K+," a tan slice labeled "N−K+," a light orange slice labeled "N−K−," and a dark orange slice labeled "N+K−." Every chart consists of exactly four slices, with the corresponding percentage labels displayed directly inside the segments in black text; no slices are visually emphasized, exploded, or offset. In the "easy" chart, the teal N+K+ slice represents 55.4%, followed by the tan N−K+ slice at 38.3%, the light orange N−K− slice at 4.6%, and the dark orange N+K− slice at 1.7%. The "medium" chart displays a similar distribution, with the teal N+K+ segment at 58.8%, tan N−K+ at 35.4%, light orange N−K− at 4.0%, and dark orange N+K− at 1.8%. The "hard" chart shows a different distribution, where the light orange N−K− slice is the largest at 37.9%, followed by the tan N−K+ slice at 37.3%, the teal N+K+ slice at 18.1%, and the dark orange N+K− slice at 6.7%. Visually, all three charts maintain the exact same clockwise sequence of color categories regardless of the varying proportional sizes.
